If we are talking about the chaos of evacuation and people fleeing, then we also need to speak honestly about what caused it.

For more than two decades, decisions made by the United States — from supporting militant structures in the region, to later handing Afghanistan over to the same group that destroyed its institutions and freedoms — played a central role in creating this crisis.
Thousands of Afghans worked with U.S. forces, trusted U.S. promises, and put their lives on the line.
When Kabul collapsed to the Taliban—your long-time regional partners—not because Afghans fled without reason, but because their lives were in immediate danger.
Many of them were allies who risked everything because they believed in the values the United States claimed to defend.
Whether one agrees or disagrees with the withdrawal strategy, one fact remains clear:
The suffering, displacement, and humiliation of millions of Afghans did not appear overnight.
It was the outcome of political decisions made by the U.S., and the empowerment of the Taliban and their sponsors.
Accountability begins with acknowledging the truth — not blaming those who became refugees because they trusted America.
